SINGLE-BINARY C++17 WAMR/QUICKJS/MCP LAN SERVER & MACOS ACCESSIBILITY APPLE PASSWORDS LAUNCHER
nwdxlgzs/HttpLocalServer (v3.5.1 C++17 + WAMR + Magika + MCP) + jessekhach/QuickPass (Zero-Disk Keychain UI)
🌐 nwdxlgzs/HttpLocalServer (★39 · Apache-2.0 · C++17 Single-Binary v3.5.1)
1. All-in-One Single Executable: SQLite FTS5 + Magika + WAMR 2.4.5 + MCP
• Embeds SQLite FTS5 trigram in-memory index (up to 250,000 items / 64MiB / 60s background swap)
• Static WAMR 2.4.5 + QuickJS-NG + Magika content inference + MCP (2026-07-28 spec + legacy compat)
2. Version-Pinned Range Resume (409 Guard) & Application-Layer CoW
Version-Pinned URL → Binds size + mtime; returns HTTP 409 if file changes mid-download
App-Layer CoW → Flushes temp file without global write lock; old handles keep old version
Path & Symlink Sec → openat/O_NOFOLLOW + blocks Windows ADS, symlinks & reparse points
Isolated Write → /_clients/<TCP_IP>/ per-IP sandbox (ignores spoofable X-Forwarded-For)
3. Slowloris Drain Cap, DNS-Rebinding Guard & Zero-CDN Offline UI
• Rejected upload drain strictly capped at 64 KiB & 1s absolute deadline (defeats slow-drip attacks)
• Write token endpoint enforces numeric IP / localhost Host check to block DNS rebinding
• Built-in Monaco editor, Office/PDF/PPT viewer & optional P2P WebRTC/Range cache (max 64MiB)
Architectural Takeaway for AI Solution Architects:
Standard HTTP Range servers silently splice old and new bytes when a file updates mid-transfer.
HttpLocalServer's version-pinned 409 URLs, application-layer CoW, TCP-peer IP isolation, and
embedded WAMR+QuickJS+MCP runtime turn one C++17 binary into a hardened LAN appliance.
🔑 jessekhach/QuickPass (★39 · GPL-3.0 · Swift macOS 15+ Apple Passwords UI)
1. Bridging an API-Less System App via macOS Accessibility Tree
• Apple Passwords has no public SDK: QuickPass drives it invisibly via macOS Accessibility API
• Global ⌃⌥Space overlay with instant search, ⌘C user, ⇧⌘C password, ⌥⌘C 2FA & ⌘↩ / ⌥⌘↩ autofill
2. Zero-Clipboard Reveal Read & Field-by-Field Write Verification
Hidden Reveal Read → Triggers Reveal Password while hidden, reads AX value & re-masks immediately
Read-Back Save Gate → Fills New Password form field-by-field & verifies every field before saving
2-Min RAM-Only TTL → Secrets never touch disk; purged after 2m, Lock Now, screen lock or sleep
Concealed Clipboard → Marks copied secrets concealed (skipped by history apps) + 60s auto-clear
3. Zero-Third-Party Favicon Privacy & EdDSA + Notarized Updates
• Fetches website icons directly from each target domain (never leaks login list to 3rd-party icon APIs)
• Reads current tab URL across Safari, Chrome, Arc, Brave, Edge & Vivaldi for instant site matching
• Sparkle updates verified with both Apple Developer ID notarization and EdDSA cryptographic signatures
Architectural Takeaway for AI Solution Architects:
When automating closed system apps via Accessibility APIs, never route secrets through the
system clipboard by default (read AX Reveal state while hidden), mark intentional copies as
concealed with a 60s TTL, and enforce field-by-field read-back before committing UI mutations.
